advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test for referencing_commits when build_resolver_scan_index returns None (unreadable tracker root), asserting resolution falls back to per-call scanning and still credits the target commit.
evidence: Added lines: `scan_index = build_resolver_scan_index(tracker)` then `alias_index = scan_index.alias_to_dirs if scan_index is not None else None` / `dir_names = scan_index.sorted_dir_names if scan_index is not None else None`
Comment on the added lines: "`None` (tracker unreadable) falls back to per-call scanning, preserving behavior."

ABSENCE: search of tests/ for `build_resolver_scan_index`, `_scan_tracker_root`, and `ResolverScanIndex` finds only the happy-path parity test at test_attach_commits.py:340; no test exercises the None-return / fallback path.
Named violating input: a tracker_dir that os.listdir cannot read (e.g. a path pointing at a nonexistent directory), which makes build_resolver_scan_index return None.
advisory.finding: The newly added None-fallback branch in referencing_commits (`alias_index = scan_index.alias_to_dirs if scan_index is not None else None` and the parallel `dir_names` assignment) is untested: no test drives referencing_commits with an unreadable/nonexistent tracker root so that build_resolver_scan_index returns None and resolution falls back to per-call scanning. A regression that broke the ternary (e.g. dropping the None guard, causing an AttributeError on None, or passing a non-None dir_names when the index build failed) would not be caught.
scenarios: An impact-present close run where the tracker root becomes unreadable mid-history walk must still credit commits via per-call scanning.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that monkeypatches os.listdir to raise OSError for the tracker root (or points at a nonexistent tracker), then calls referencing_commits and asserts the alias-credited target_sha is still found via the per-call fallback.
